hook.line: A Canadian team spent 18 years computing until, in 2007, they proved that perfect play is a draw — one of the largest games ever solved.
hook.say: Let’s jump into the history of checkers!

ch.say: It was born when two games merged.
p: Around the 12th century in France, alquerque pieces are said to have been moved onto a chessboard.
By the 16th century the “you must capture” rule took hold, and the game split into British, Dutch, Russian and other rule sets.

ch.say: In the end, a computer found the answer.
tl: A game on the chessboard is said to arise in France
First English book on the game (William Payne)
Marion Tinsley reigns as the world’s best
The program Chinook plays in the human world title match
The Chinook team proves it is a draw

ch.say: If you can capture, you must!
p: Pieces move one square diagonally forward and capture by jumping.
Reach the far row and you are crowned a king that can also move backward.

ch.say: Each country has its own rules.
cards: 10×10 with 20 pieces each; kings fly along diagonals
8×8; flying kings, and men may capture backward
An unusual relative whose pieces move orthogonally

ch.say: The best human and the best machine.
cards: A mathematician and the world’s best for over 40 years, said to have lost only a handful of games
A University of Alberta program, among the first computers to play a human world champion

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: Same game: Americans say checkers, the British say draughts
Only the dark ones — pieces always stay on one colour

p: Simple rules, 900 years of wisdom. Make your first move.
